prose_updates.tldr: A single endpoint-safe joint logistic series fit now enforces binary coherence and has score \( (A-\pi_1)v \) and information \(E_P(\pi_0\pi_1vw)\). On the canonical chart, the profiled two-boundary Gram calculation proves the signed Hall-functional rate, with global Hessian scale \(J_n^{\alpha_\star+1}/n\), and the weighted conditional-variance calculation proves \(D_{a,n}=o_P(1)\) under the amplified tail schedule. Under the resulting explicit tuning window, the compensated heavy law, the corrected learned-propensity Gaussian influence expansion, the moving two-arm QTE law, and refitted arm-vector pointwise and finite-quantile simultaneous inference follow. The raw scalar comparison is only a defined internal diagnostic.

project_justification.gap: Regular series-logit and QTE theory does not provide the two-endpoint Hall-weighted signed-Riesz and weighted evaluation-variance calculations needed by a learned weak-overlap quantile estimator.
project_justification.niche: The causal QTE remains identified by the known adjustment functional; the contribution is feasible noncritical limit and coverage theory with a binary-coherent first stage, compensated heavy tails, and a moving two-arm row law.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the canonical-chart profiled information bounds, the heavy signed-functional and conditional evaluation rates, the three Gaussian weighted-variance regimes, samplewise approximation to an explicit symmetric oracle arm vector, moving-law recombination, and complete-subsample pointwise and maximum-band calibration.

sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary and both fitted arm probabilities come from one joint log odds, so they sum to one pointwise. Uniform conclusions remain restricted to noncritical gamma-separated scheduled laws.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: At sample size \(N=n\) and every refit size \(N=m\), each fold fits the same compact-coefficient, ridged logistic series with clipped canonical log coordinates and no global probability-range constraint. Heavy schedules satisfy the signed mean and amplified tail conditions in the corrected likelihood lemma; Gaussian schedules satisfy its global Hessian condition, \(\sqrt N J_N^{-2s}\to0\), and \(J_N\log J_N/\sqrt N\to0\).

prose_updates.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky provide an observed-true-propensity weak-overlap quantile benchmark; Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder and Firpo provide regular estimated-propensity benchmarks. Ma and Wang and Khan and Tamer are retained only as limited-overlap and support-condition background. Knight is the source of the classical check-loss decomposition, which is reverified here, and Politis, Romano, and Wolf provide general subsampling context; neither supplies the paper-specific learned-propensity coupling. Dorn is weak-overlap nuisance-tail context, while Sant'Anna, Song, and Xu is propensity-balance context. No cited theorem is asserted to prove the new two-endpoint spline calculation, and the raw scalar diagnostic is not attributed to a published procedure.
prose_updates.interpretation: The joint likelihood has finite information because both endpoints are weighted by \(\pi_0\pi_1\). The maximal endpoint exponent governs global Hessian stability, while the target arm exponent governs its signed Riesz norm. Heavy oracle transfer balances the fitted tail error on \(M_n/h_{a,n}\); the correctly weighted conditional variance then decays as \(M_n^{-(\alpha_a-1)/\alpha_a}\). In regular arms the exact evaluation variance splits at \(\alpha_a=1/2\). Armwise oracle standardization followed by full-sample recombination is what preserves the moving QTE mixture.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The model is restricted to the canonical one-dimensional uniform boundary chart, the reported quantile set is finite, and uniformity excludes a neighborhood of \(\gamma=2\). The heavy tuning interval is explicit but can be empty for some highly asymmetric endpoint-exponent and smoothness combinations; conclusions apply exactly where the displayed \(\xi,\lambda\) inequalities hold at both \(N=n\) and \(N=m\). Simultaneous coverage is only over the fixed finite \(\mathcal T\) and uses the declared maximum-law anti-concentration modulus. The separate critical fold-labelled law remains outside this result.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established result is a feasible row-wise limit and inference theorem on the canonical-chart, gamma-separated scheduled class. The heavy branch requires \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\) and the displayed signed-functional mean rate; its conditional evaluation variance is derived explicitly. The Gaussian branch uses the exact weighted reciprocal-error variance. The normalized QTE is compared samplewise to an explicit symmetric oracle arm vector before its law is compared with \(Z_{P,n}\). Refitted arm-vector subsampling then gives uniform asymmetric pointwise and finite-quantile simultaneous coverage. No claim is made at \(\gamma=2\), for an infinite quantile process, outside the explicit tuning region, or against a published raw scalar procedure.
